abstract: Although the amplitude estimation of sinusoids is a linear and tractable problem when their frequencies are known, the accuracy of signal modeling is fundamentally limited by the inevitable frequency mismatches produced by existing methods. Quasi-harmonic modeling (QHM) and its extensions (aQHM and eaQHM) offer the ability to refine frequency estimates while extracting amplitudes; however, their extraction and correction capabilities remain limited. In this paper, we first revisit QHM methods from the perspective of frequency mismatches, and reveal that their performances are essentially constrained by the order of the model. Specifically, QHM methods are linear models and thus incapable of capturing higher-order frequency variations, leading to suboptimal modeling accuracy. Second, to address this limitation, we propose a higher-order modeling framework that enables more precise approximation of signal components. Eventually, we qualitatively characterize the optimization problem and employ the Levenberg--Marquardt (LM) algorithm for parameter estimation. As a result, the proposed method allows for significantly improved estimation of amplitudes, frequencies, and phases of sinusoidal components, enabling more accurate signal modeling. Experiments on both simulation study and speech signals demonstrate the superiority of the high-order model in frequency refinement and parameter extraction and its robustness under additive noise conditions.
